newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says gets green light for EU trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says gets green light for EU trade talks.

text.p: Mexico on Monday said it had been given the go-ahead by European Union ministers to begin negotiations for a political, economic and trade pact that it hopes will sharply boost trans-Atlantic commerce.
"In coming days, the Mexican government will table talks with the EU authorities to set the date to begin negotiations, which could be at the start of June," the Trade Ministry said in a statement.
It said the EU Council of Ministers had given the mandate to the European Commission to negotiate the pact, ending a long hold-up over the way the deal was to be negotiated.

The European Commission had proposed discussing the political pact first, and coming to trade later. But Mexico, wary of interference in its internal affairs, said it would only accept negotiations that were carried out on trade and politics at the same time.
It said a compromise was finally reached suitable to both sides. Last week, Mexican Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria bowed to EU insistence on including a human rights clause in the eventual deal.

Mexico has been ruled for 68 years by the Institutional Revolutionary Party, which has often been accused of using electoral fraud to retain power. In 1994 the country signed a free trade pact with the United States and Canada and it has been eager to court Europe ever since.
